title: What is known about 1RB1LC_0RC0RB_1LD0LA_1LE---_1LF1RA_1LA1LC
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB1LC_0RC0RB_1LD0LA_1LE---_1LF1RA_1LA1LC.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
The tape holds two binary counters, U up and V down. When V runs out the machine rebuilds V from the bottom digits of U; the rebuild is now computed exactly as a map on the counters.
verdict: Decided by an outside Rocq proof: it never halts. Busycoq pull request 58 (Dennis Koshta, 2026-11-05) proves this in Rocq, and we compiled it here with Coq 8.20.1 on busycoq's BB6 branch: its only axiom is functional extensionality from Coq's standard library (Print Assumptions), and its transition table is this machine. The file proves it for the left-right mirror image and transfers it with busycoq's flip lemma. It is their proof, on busycoq's definitions of a machine and of halting, and busycoq's maintainer has not yet reviewed it. Everything else on this page is what this repository found on its own, which by itself leaves the question open.

The question is open here. Lean proves the ticks; the exact macro map finds no halt in the first 109624 steps, and every halt it can produce comes from one walk over the counter's digits running off its top.
Where a halt would come from. Only from a rebuild after V reaches 0; which rebuilds halt is listed for small counters.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (D1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: The tick rules of the two counters
claims.text: For each of the headers 0110101, 0110111 the run uses, two theorems: with V odd, L 00000 (00001)^j 00 D>0110101 01 R becomes L 00001 (00000)^j 00 D>0110101 11 R in 10 * j + 38 steps; with V having i + 1 trailing zeros, L 00000 (00001)^j 00 D>0110101 (11)^(i+1) 01 R becomes L 00001 (00000)^j 00 D>0110101 (01)^(i+1) 11 R in 8 * i + 10 * j + 46 steps. That is U + 1 and V − 1 for every number j of carries and i + 1 of borrows and every tape L, R beyond (proved along the symbolic run of tools/py/bbtools/symtm.py).

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 178 cells have been visited and 50 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: The macro map and its simulator
claims.text: At each moment V reaches 0 the tape is the clean configuration 0^inf F U 00 D> H (11)^n 1 0^inf (F the counter's top word), so the state is (H, n, N) with N the up-counter read as one number. py/rebuild.py writes that tape, runs the rebuild (tick runs of its sub-phases jumped by the proved tick rules, the rest cell by cell in C) to the next clean tick configuration (H', n', N', V'), and then adds the V' ticks of the phase by arithmetic: next state (H', n', N' + V'), steps by the closed formula of the tick costs. Tested: its first 4 states and step counts, up to about 1054 steps, equal those of py/counters.py (itself tested against tools/c/tmrun.c).

claims.title: A faster exact rebuild
claims.text: py/fastrebuild.py runs the same exact rebuild as rebuild.py (tick runs jumped by the proved tick rules, the rest cell by cell), but its C loop stops only where state D reads 0 between the gap and one of the two headers, instead of at each of the millions of 0s it reads in state D, and it decodes and rewrites the counters with byte slices. Rebuild 6 from blank tape (V of 2,176 digits) took more than 25 minutes and takes 4 s. Tested: the first 7 macro states from blank tape (to about 10991 steps) equal those of the family's own code, state by state.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9624</sup> steps (macro run)
claims.text: The macro run from blank tape goes through 9 rebuilds without a halt; at the end V has 31,967 digits and the step count is about 10<sup>9624</sup>. The run uses the faster exact rebuild below (rebuild 8 takes 18 s).

claims.title: Four kinds of rebuild, two of them in closed form
claims.text: Write the counter as its top word (1 or 1000x) and L digits U. A (header 0110101, top 1) reads every digit: new header 0110111, top 10000, all L digits 0, V gains 1 digit, and δ = 2L − U, so V' = 2n+1 − 2L + U. C (header 0110111, top 1) reads the j digits of a walk from the bottom: a first pair 01 or 10 stops it (j = 2); otherwise add 1 to U if its lowest pair is 11 and stop at the first pair whose upper digit is 1 (j = 2k). Then the new header is 0110101, the top 10000 over L − j zero digits, V gains 5j/2 + 1 digits and δ = c + 2L−j − (U >> j), with c depending only on the j digits read (U >> j > 0). B (header 0110111, top 1000x) and D (header 0110101, top 1000x) read every digit and leave N' = 2. Checked against the exact rebuild: A and C for every U < 210 with n − L in {0, 1, 3}; in the run, A twice and C three times (walks of 34, 444 and 8,182 digits), all as stated.

claims.title: Where the rebuilds halt: the walk runs off the top
claims.text: For every U < 2L, L = 3 .. 9, both values of x and n − L in {0, 1, 2, 3} (112 cases): B halts exactly for the U whose walk (the one of C) does not stop below the top of U (the all-ones U aside), when x = 0 or L is even, and never when x = 1 and L is odd; D never halts when n − L ≥ 2, and with n − L = 1 halts exactly where B does when L is even and never when L is odd. A never halts (every U < 210), nor did C for any U < 214 with n = L + 1. (D with n − L = 0 has other halting sets; no D rebuild of the run has n = L.) So the run halts only at a B or D rebuild whose counter has no 1 in the upper place of any pair, after the walk's carry. That is the invariant of the outside proof: busycoq PR 58's walls carry marked 1 bs, a 1 at an odd position of the digits.

claims.title: The walks in the run
claims.text: The kinds follow each other as A, B, C, D, then A or C again (D went to A once and to C once). The two B rebuilds of the run stopped their walk after 12 of 23 and 444 of 619 digits; the D rebuild with n − L = 1 (L = 3,286, even) after 16. A halt needs a walk that runs off the top, which for random digits has probability about 2<sup>−L/2</sup>, and L grows about threefold per rebuild. A heuristic only, now superseded by the outside proof.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: Not decided by this repository (the outside Rocq proof of busycoq PR 58 decides it). The kinds A and C are in closed form apart from the constant c of C, and the halting rebuilds are described for small counters; what is missing here is c as a formula, the maps of B and D, and a proof of any of it in Lean.

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the exact macro simulation (9 rebuilds).
Tick rules proved in Lean for every carry and borrow.

sections.heading: Two binary counters on one tape
html: Run the machine for a while and the tape sorts itself into two numbers written in binary. On the far left, after a single 1 that acts as a sentinel, is a counter U whose digits are blocks of 5 cells: 00000 is a 0 and 00001 a 1, most significant digit on the left. Then come a short gap 00, the head in state D, and a fixed header such as 0110101. Right of the header is a second counter V whose digits are pairs, least significant first: 01 is a 1 and 11 a 0.
The tick configuration is 1 U 00 D>0110101 V. Every tick adds 1 to U and takes 1 from V. Most of the time nothing else happens.

sections.heading: One tick: U + 1, V − 1
html: The head walks left through the trailing 1-digits of U, turning them into 0-digits (the carries), writes a 1-digit, then walks right to V and turns its trailing 0-pairs into 1-pairs and its lowest 1-pair into a 0-pair (the borrows). Written with j carries and i + 1 borrows:

beforeaftersteps
L 00000 (00001)^j 00 D>0110101 01 RL 00001 (00000)^j 00 D>0110101 11 R10 * j + 38
L 00000 (00001)^j 00 D>0110101 (11)^(i+1) 01 RL 00001 (00000)^j 00 D>0110101 (01)^(i+1) 11 R8 * i + 10 * j + 46

These two shapes are proved in Lean for every j and i (lean/Rules.lean), for every header the run has used (0110101, 0110111). Because the cost of a tick depends only on the numbers of carries and borrows, a long run of ticks has an exact cost: the sum of the trailing zeros of the numbers U+1, ..., U+k and V−k+1, ..., V, which has a closed form. The accelerated simulator uses it to skip billions of ticks at once.

sections.heading: The rebuild as a function of the counter
html: When V reaches 0 the tape is clean, 0^inf F U G S>H (11)^n 1 0^inf, and the machine's state is (H, n, N): header, length of V, and the up-counter read as one number together with its top word F. The rebuild then runs to the next clean tick configuration (H', n', N', V'), and the phase adds V' to the counter: the next state is (H', n', N' + V').

Here the counter's top word F is either 1 or 1000x. In the six rebuilds computed, those with top word 1 left only a two-digit counter N' (2 or 3), so the next counter, 2n' + N' − δ, is written almost entirely by the rebuild.

sections.heading: Halting, reduced to the rebuild map
html: Ticks never halt, so a halt can only come from a rebuild. The exhaustive runs of the rebuild for small counters list the ones that halt; whether the run from blank tape ever feeds one of them is the open question, now a question about the macro map on (H, n, N) rather than about the raw machine.

family: Up/down two counters with resets (G12 family 3b)
summary: Up/down counters with proved ticks; four kinds of rebuild, and a halt only where a walk over the digits of U runs off its top (checked for small counters); exact macro map, no halt in ~10^9624 steps. Decided outside: busycoq PR 58 proves in Rocq that it never halts (compiled here).
